title: 11.2 A Blocker-Tolerant Receiver with VCO-Based Non-Uniform Multi-Level Time-Approximation Filter with -36dB EVM in 28nm CMOS
problem: Crowded spectrum creates out-of-band (OOB) and alias-band blockers that degrade in-band EVM after sampling. Prior time-approximation-filtering (TAF) and N-path filter designs have limited blocker rejection and reconfigurability.
motivation: Increasingly crowded wireless spectrum and dense signal environments require high-order filtering with tunable response and reconfigurability to reject multiple classes of blockers (far-out, nearby, alias-band) without costly switched-capacitor arrays.
method: Out-of-band and alias-band blockers—strong interfering signals from nearby frequencies—corrupt the signal quality after it's converted to digital form. This receiver prevents that using a mixer-first architecture followed by three filtering techniques: multilevel time-approximation filtering (sampling at irregular, precisely chosen intervals rather than uniform clock ticks), a VCO-based integrator with embedded digitalization (which simultaneously collects and converts signal energy), and non-uniform N-path filtering. Time-gated integration patterns—which change when signal collection occurs—allow it to suppress multiple types of blockers at once. The result is 65dB of blocker rejection while maintaining reconfigurability and low implementation cost in 28nm CMOS.
key_novelty: Combining multilevel time-approximation filtering with a VCO-based integrator (which simultaneously collects signal energy and converts it to digital form) achieves 65dB of blocker rejection while keeping the receiver reconfigurable and inexpensive.
contributions: Multilevel time-approximation filtering (mTAF) for multiple blocker suppression
VCO-based integrator improving TAF accuracy at reduced cost vs. switched-capacitor designs
Combined N-path and non-uniform sampling for far-out and alias-band blocker rejection
Nearly 20dB improvement over prior N-path and TAF receivers
primary_theme: blocker-tolerant receiver with multi-level time-approximation filtering
